title: Ultrasound-guided blocks for the hand: median, ulnar, radial and digital
short: Forearm and digital blocks for the hand
summary: Hand injuries are among the commonest emergency department procedures. Learn to block the median, ulnar and superficial radial nerves in the forearm and the digital nerves in the finger with ultrasound, using small volumes, after a careful examination and within a safe system.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency and acute care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and emergency nurse practitioners who perform, or are training to perform, ultrasound-guided blocks for hand procedures under their trust's governance.
outcomes: Examine and document hand nerve and tendon function before any block
Set up a safe block: consent, dose calculation, monitoring, Stop Before You Block and documentation
Find the median, ulnar and superficial radial nerves in the forearm and tell them from tendons and vessels
Choose the right block, or combination, for a wound from the sensory map of the hand
Perform an ultrasound-guided digital block with small paired deposits
references: Liebmann O, Price D, Mills C, et al. Feasibility of forearm ultrasonography-guided nerve blocks of the radial, ulnar, and median nerves for hand procedures in the emergency department. Annals of Emergency Medicine. 2006;48:558-62.
